short_description: VitiBot builds Bakus, an electric autonomous straddle tractor (enjambeur) for vineyard row work, sold into Champagne and other French wine regions. The company is owned by SDF Group, the Italian tractor manufacturer. VitiBot's public site describes full autonomy and worker safety benefits but does not disclose the perception stack, so no computer vision or machine learning claim is verified here; treat it as autonomous machinery until the navigation technology is documented. It matters to the wine data landscape as one of the main European sources of in row robotic operating data.

name: Kegshoe
ai_use_case: keg fleet tracking / sales CRM
short_description: Keg tracking and management software plus a sales CRM for breweries: scan-based fills, deliveries, returns and lookups across the keg fleet, with inventory levels and pickup timing. Founded 2015 by Torin Regier and Adrian Pawliszko. Kegshoe makes no public AI or machine-learning claims; it is tracked here as the system of record for keg fleet and account data, not as an AI vendor.

name: Kaspar Schulz
ai_use_case: brewhouse process control / cloud maintenance
short_description: The world's oldest brewing plant manufacturer, ten generations family-owned, building brewhouses, malting systems and distillery plants. Its Pioneer Pro control system is marketed as intelligent process control with innovative automation and cloud-based maintenance management, alongside the web-based SCHULZ app for remote plant control. Kaspar Schulz makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as the plant and control layer that brewing process data originates from, not as an AI vendor.

name: Anton Paar
ai_use_case: inline and lab beverage measurement
short_description: Measurement instruments for beverage quality control: the Alcolyzer alcohol meter, CarboQC dissolved-CO2 meter, density meters and modular packaged-beer measurement systems used inline, at-line and in the lab across beer, wine, spirits and RTDs. Over 40 years in beverage analysis. Anton Paar makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as the measurement layer that brewery and winery quality data originates from, not as an AI vendor.

name: Meura
ai_use_case: mash filtration and brewhouse technology
short_description: Brewing and distilling process technology, best known for the Meura 2001 thin-bed membrane mash filter, used in production of more than 25 percent of global beer volume; the 500th unit sold in 2023. Founded 1845 by Jean-Baptiste Meura; a Boccard subsidiary since the Boccard family entered the shareholding in 1987. Meura makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as brewhouse process technology, not as an AI vendor.

name: Worter
ai_use_case: brewery ERP / mass-balance recipe engine
short_description: Grain-to-glass brewery management ERP for craft breweries and fermentation businesses: equipment register with auto QR tagging, batch lifecycle records, inventory with PAR and expiry alerts, QC approvals, and a mass-balance based recipe engine that calculates expected COGS as a recipe is built and flags process deviations against recipe intent in real time. Worter Technologies Private Limited, CIN U62013PN2024PTC234801, incorporated 7 October 2024 in Pune; directors Shaju Balakrishnan and Kranti Satyanarayan Mamidpalliwar. Worter makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as an Indian brewery system of record, not as an AI vendor.

name: Praj Industries
ai_use_case: AI-enabled precision fermentation / brewery plant engineering
short_description: Process solutions company for bio-energy, high-purity water and brewery plants, with a brewery division running since 1994, over 70 percent market share in India and installations across Africa and Southeast Asia. In 2025 Praj opened an Advanced Precision Fermentation Lab at its Praj Matrix R&D centre in Pune with a research partnership with BRIC-NCCS, designed to support high-capacity AI-enabled fermentation processes across food, pharma, biofuels and beverages, aimed at reducing scale-up risk and improving process reliability. The AI claim attaches to the fermentation R&D facility, not to the brewery plant product line.

name: ProLeiT
ai_use_case: brewery process control and MES
short_description: Software manufacturer of the PLC-based process control systems Plant iT and brewmaxx, with MES built in: integrated process visualisation, pre-configured automation objects, ISA-88 compliant batch systems and continuous recipe and materials management, running on Schneider Electric, Siemens and Rockwell controllers. brewmaxx is one of the most widely installed brewery process control systems. Part of Schneider Electric. ProLeiT makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as the process control and MES layer that brewery batch data originates from, not as an AI vendor.

name: Konvoy Kegs
ai_use_case: iot keg fleet tracking
short_description: Konvoy rents, services and tracks kegs for brewers across Australia, New Zealand and the UK, and describes itself as operating the largest IoT tracked keg fleet globally with automated location tracking on every keg and no scanning required. The trackers were built by UnaBiz on the Sigfox 0G network operated by Thinxtra, and report keg location, temperature and usage. Konvoy makes no machine learning claim: the platform is asset telemetry and fleet visibility rather than modelling.

name: BinaryBeer
ai_use_case: smart keg supply chain insights
short_description: BinaryBeer builds KegLink, a low power IoT device that turns a keg into a tracked container reporting location, temperature and beer freshness, plus the Binary Cloud platform that brewers use for fleet maps, alerts and reporting. The company states the platform is "powered by machine learning and AI-driven algorithms" that "continuously refine its insights" for fleet activity and supply chain optimisation, though it does not name the models or specific predictions. Asahi Europe and International selected BinaryBeer for an international smart keg deployment, and the product is also sold in North America through a partnership with Kegshoe.

name: MicroStar Logistics
ai_use_case: shared keg pool logistics
short_description: MicroStar runs the largest shared keg pool in the beer industry on a pay per fill model, so brewers use pooled kegs instead of owning a fleet, and it claims to remove 4.1 million truck miles of empty keg returns a year. Its international arm is Kegstar, which serves brewers in the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand and offers a customer platform called TAP. MicroStar makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site: it is a physical keg logistics network with a customer portal, and it is included here because it is the incumbent that owns most of the keg movement data in the sector.
key_people: Michael Hranicka (President and CEO), Bryan Place (President, Kegstar), Harley Green (VP Technology and Customer Experience)

name: KegChek
ai_use_case: keg and draught asset tracking
short_description: KegChek is a keg tracking and fleet management system for breweries, operated by UBC COOL CANADA INC, part of the UBC Group. It tracks kegs by barcode, QR, RFID and Bluetooth scans at each stage of keg rotation and shows location and status on a map, and it extends the same tracking to trade marketing and dispensing assets such as tap handles, jockey boxes, kegerators and patio umbrellas. The product makes no AI or machine learning claim: reporting is standard inventory and status reporting exported to PDF or Excel.

name: Kegtron
ai_use_case: keg level and pour monitoring
short_description: Kegtron makes inline smart keg monitors that sit between the keg and the tap, using a flowmeter and a wireless processor to report how much beer has been dispensed and how much remains, for both home kegerators and multi tap venues. Products are the Kegtron Pro and Gen 1 lines plus SAFECID line cleaners, and the platform adds reporting and an Untappd integration. Kegtron makes no AI or machine learning claim: the value is direct volume measurement and real time reporting.

name: KegSpeed
ai_use_case: cellular smart keg trackers
short_description: KegSpeed sells patented smart trackers that attach to any keg brand and report location and status over cellular and GPS, with embedded sensors for motion, temperature and pressure, aimed at brewers and distributors trying to cut keg loss. It positions itself as an open system with an API that works across keg makers and brewery inventory software rather than a closed fleet. KegSpeed makes no AI or machine learning claim: it refers only to analytics and data insights on top of the tracker feed.

name: KegID
ai_use_case: keg scan tracking and traceability
short_description: KegID is a low cost keg tracking subscription, run by the Hillebrand keg team inside DHL, that lets brewery staff scan kegs with a smartphone camera and see fleet location, keg age and days in circulation. It covers batch traceability and quality control reporting and integrates with the Kegspediter keg management service. Pricing runs from USD 25 a month for 150 kegs to USD 100 a month for 500 or more. KegID makes no AI or machine learning claim: it is barcode scanning plus reporting.

name: TrackAbout
ai_use_case: returnable asset and keg tracking
short_description: TrackAbout, now a Datacor product, is a returnable asset tracking platform whose named verticals include beer kegs alongside industrial gas cylinders and pallets. It covers keg lifecycle visibility, mobile scanning and photo capture at delivery, maintenance and inspection workflow, rental billing calculation and a customer portal showing asset and delivery history. The keg product makes no AI or predictive analytics claim; Datacor markets a separate Datacor AI offering that is not described as part of TrackAbout.

name: eProvenance
ai_use_case: wine cold chain scoring
short_description: eProvenance is a Franco American company that monitors the temperature and shipping conditions of fine wine at container, pallet or case level, using sensors placed in shipments and analysis of the resulting condition data. Its proprietary scientific algorithm converts a shipment temperature history into the eProvenance Score, a 0 to 100 rating of whether the wine stayed fresh or was heat damaged. In 2020 it launched VinAssure, a wine supply chain platform built on IBM Blockchain Transparent Supply. The scoring algorithm is described as scientific and rule based rather than machine learning, and the company makes no explicit ML claim.

name: Hillebrand Gori
ai_use_case: beverage freight and cold chain logistics
short_description: Hillebrand Gori, part of DHL, is the dominant specialist logistics provider for wine, beer and spirits, moving cased and bulk beverage by sea, rail, road and air, including temperature controlled transport, flexitanks, ISO tanks, warehousing and a control tower service. Its digital layer is the myHillebrandGori platform for shipment booking and tracking plus a carbon calculator that compares emissions across shipping scenarios, and it also runs the KegID keg tracking product. It makes no AI or machine learning claim, and is included because it sits on more beverage supply chain movement data than any pure software vendor in this surface.

name: Cellr
ai_use_case: serialised bottle track and trace
short_description: Cellr gives wine and spirits producers serialised QR codes and NFC or RFID enabled lids and labels applied on the bottling line, creating a per bottle digital identity used for anti counterfeit verification, track and trace, digital product passport compliance and direct to consumer engagement. Brand dashboards report scan, claim and conversion analytics, with published customer results such as Red Hill Estate averaging 250 bottles claimed per month. Cellr makes no AI or machine learning claim: the platform is serialisation, authentication and engagement reporting.

name: Waterplan
ai_use_case: water risk and replenishment modelling
short_description: Waterplan is a water risk platform that combines a site's operational data with hydrological models and satellite remote sensing to quantify water risk in financial terms and validate volumetric water benefits from replenishment projects. Its own case study covers Ambev, the AB InBev brewing subsidiary in South America, which uses the platform to measure and validate watershed and restoration projects in three high water risk basins and to auto-generate the evidence log for sustainability reporting. The company describes itself as an AI native platform and cites AI agents for data collection and anomaly detection in resource use; the substantive modelling described is hydrological plus remote sensing rather than a named ML model. Y Combinator Summer 2021.
key_people: Jose Ignacio Galindo (Co-founder and CEO), Nicolas Wertheimer (Co-founder)

name: Zevero
ai_use_case: automated scope 3 emission factor matching
short_description: Zevero is a carbon accounting and ESG reporting platform that measures scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions and produces CSRD, SECR and CDP disclosures. It has an unusually deep drinks customer base and names Northern Monk, DEYA Brewing, Stroud Brewery, Brixton Brewery, JUBEL Beer, Yakima Chief Hops, Asahi and the sake producers Suigei and Manotsuru on its own site. The AI claim is specific and modest: AI driven emission factor matching and document extraction that reads uploaded invoices and utility documents in multiple languages, applied to fermentation related scope 3 lines. It integrates with BrewMan brewery management software so purchase and delivery data flows in automatically.

name: ClimateHound
ai_use_case: carbon footprint accounting for drinks producers
short_description: ClimateHound is a carbon footprint and decarbonisation reporting platform aimed squarely at small and mid sized drinks producers. Its winery page names customers including pleb urban winery, Wanderlust Wine Co, Cellarest, Old Elk Distillery, Montanya Distillers, 3BR Distillery and Bauman's Cider, and it pulls data through more than 200 integrations with business tools and utility providers. It makes no machine learning claim anywhere on the site: this is integration driven emissions accounting and reporting, not modelling. Included because it is one of the few carbon platforms with a genuinely wine and spirits native customer list.

name: Cambrian Innovation
ai_use_case: remote monitoring of brewery wastewater treatment
short_description: Cambrian Innovation is an MIT spinout that treats brewery and winery effluent on site with bioelectrically enhanced anaerobic systems, EcoVolt and BlueCycle MBR, recovering biogas and reuse water, and sells it as a Water Energy Purchase Agreement so the producer puts up no capital. Its own site names Anheuser Busch Houston, Russian River Brewing, Bear Republic Brewing, Northern United Brewing and Rombauer Vineyards as customers, and Lagunitas in Petaluma has run an EcoVolt system since 2014 under a ten year operations agreement. The digital layer is cloud based real time monitoring and analytics of reactor operation; the company makes no machine learning claim. Relevant to the water stewardship and effluent side of beverage ESG.

name: Aquacycl
ai_use_case: remote real time control of modular wastewater reactors
short_description: Aquacycl treats ultra high strength food and beverage wastewater at source with BETT, a modular bioelectrochemical reactor using electrochemically active bacteria, avoiding dilution and cutting sludge. Every reactor is remotely monitored and controlled in real time from Aquacycl, which removes the need for a full time onsite operator, and probe data is used to read microbial colony health. Its own brewery case study documents 99 percent BOD and 85 percent TSS removal at Joshua Tree Brewery, and PepsiCo is named on the site; the company has also worked through AB InBev's 100+ Accelerator. No machine learning claim is made: this is instrumented process control, not modelling.

name: Zero Carbon Forum
ai_use_case: sector carbon benchmarking and reduction roadmaps
short_description: Zero Carbon Forum is a not for profit collaborative representing over a third of the UK brewing and hospitality sector across roughly 35,000 sites, providing carbon footprinting, benchmarking, sector roadmaps and carbon coaching rather than software. Named brewer members include Adnams, St Austell Brewery, Gipsy Hill Brewing, Thornbridge Brewery, Stewart Brewing and Wells and Co, with BrewDog, Fuller's, Greene King, Marston's, Shepherd Neame and Young's cited in trade coverage of the membership. It launched a brewing sector specific decarbonisation roadmap in 2022 and partners with Mondra for product level carbon data. It makes no AI or machine learning claim; it matters here because it is where a large slice of UK brewing emissions data is actually pooled and benchmarked.
key_people: Mark Chapman (Founder and CEO), Bob Gordon (Director)

name: Provenate
ai_use_case: chat assistant over distillery production and duty data
short_description: Provenate is an all in one production, stock, duty and compliance system built specifically for whisky distilleries and bottlers, replacing spreadsheets and manual HMRC duty returns and holding a full audit trail from wash to spirit yield and cask. It names Ardnamurchan Distillery and Adelphi Distillery as customers; Ardnamurchan uses it to digitise its operational flow and to back consumer facing provenance claims, including sourcing and climate impact of the liquid, via a bottle QR code. The only AI in the product is an assistant that lets staff query their own cask stock and duty data in natural language; there is no carbon accounting or LCA engine, so treat this as a system of record with a provenance and reporting layer.

name: NIRAS
ai_use_case: brewery discrete event simulation and digital twin, plus industry benchmarking
short_description: Danish independent engineering consultancy with a named brewing and distilling practice covering process design, mashing and fermentation engineering, water treatment, automation and full project delivery. It runs the NIRAS Brewing Benchmark Club (NBBC), a global beer and beverage benchmarking dataset members can explore across regions and plant sizes, and sells Opti-Brew, a modelling tool that analyses production efficiency and finds process bottlenecks for expansion planning. Its Virtual Brewery offering is 3D discrete event simulation that becomes a digital twin when wired into plant MES, SCADA, PLC and IoT data. NIRAS makes no machine learning claim: the modelling described is deterministic simulation, not statistical learning.

name: Briggs of Burton
ai_use_case: no ai claim; process engineering design and build for breweries and distilleries
short_description: Process engineering contractor tracing its history to 1732, now part of the CLPT Group, designing brewhouses, cold block equipment, stills, ageing and blending processes for brewers and distillers. Named work includes Scotch whisky producers and a Mexican tequila plant running 140,000 litres per day, and it markets a combined BrewStillery technology. Services run from feasibility study through project management and commissioning. Its own site makes no artificial intelligence, machine learning or data analytics claim; it is included as an engineering layer that shapes what beverage plant data exists at all.

name: Seeq
ai_use_case: self service time series analytics and golden batch profiling on brewery process historian data
short_description: Industrial advanced analytics vendor that sits on top of process historians such as OSIsoft PI and lets process engineers cleanse, contextualise and model time series data without a data science team. Its own resource library carries a brewery use case in which engineers built a reference profile from five historically good batches, then used average plus and minus three standard deviation boundaries to flag temperature deviations during the diacetyl rest, giving early warning on batch quality when offline diacetyl results lag. The brewery case is statistical boundary monitoring rather than machine learning, though the wider platform also offers ML tooling on the same data. Seeq is a cross industry vendor, not a beverage specialist.

name: TrendMiner
ai_use_case: self service industrial time series analytics and anomaly monitoring for process plants
short_description: Belgian self service industrial analytics platform for continuous and batch process industries, offering search over historian time series, data contextualisation into events, 24/7 monitoring with alerts and, more recently, agentic AI and an Analytics Agent. Its food and beverage page covers compliance and CIP optimisation, OEE and resource efficiency, and taste and texture consistency. Named reference customers on that page are Nestle, Avebe and CP Kelco; beers and spirits are listed as coming soon, so there is no verified brewery or distillery customer yet. Included as part of the historian analytics layer that beverage plants buy, not as a proven drinks deployment.

name: Dennis Group
ai_use_case: no ai claim; food and beverage plant design build with automation and controls data integration
short_description: Design build firm working exclusively for the food and beverage industry, ranked the largest food and beverage design firm by Engineering News Record since 2015, covering process design, controls and automation and system integration. Its beverage market page lists beer and distilled spirits among its categories, with Boston Beer named as a client on an 880,000 square foot facility. One case study describes a data driven beverage facility where building management systems were integrated with process controls to generate more actionable operating data. No simulation, digital twin or machine learning product is claimed on its own site.

name: Alfa Laval
ai_use_case: iot condition monitoring and root cause analytics on brewery and beverage process equipment
short_description: Swedish process equipment maker supplying heat exchangers, separators, decanters, pumps and valves into breweries and beverage plants, with a hygienic processing product line covered by the brewing trade press. Its digital layer is CM Connect, a subscription condition monitor and 4G cloud gateway linking up to ten wireless vibration monitors, and Clariot, a sensor plus gateway plus analytics package that reports vibration, temperature and run time and returns root cause recommendations for process, installation and mechanical faults before breakdown. The published beverage reference is a Britvic bottling plant, and the site does not disclose the algorithms, so the analytics should not be read as a machine learning claim. In November 2025 Alfa Laval announced work on AI assisted heat exchanger service diagnostics.

name: Pellenc (Pera-Pellenc)
ai_use_case: connected winery press and cellar telemetry
short_description: Pellenc, through its Pera-Oenoprocess winery division, builds pneumatic presses, destemmers and cellar process equipment for wineries. Its named digital product P-Connect transmits real-time pressing data to a smartphone or PC (press state, time remaining, programme number, phase number, and juice volume in hectolitres with EasyPress 2), sends SMS alerts on cycle end and press faults, and supports remote diagnostics for after-sales assistance. The wider Pellenc Connect platform visualises machine, agronomic and oenological data from vineyard to winery. No AI or predictive maintenance claim is made.

name: BrauKon
ai_use_case: brewhouse process automation and recipe control
short_description: BrauKon is a Bavarian brewhouse and brewery plant OEM serving craft and mid-size breweries. It ships two named control products: BrauControl, a full brewery process automation system covering malt intake through to bright beer tank and CIP, with 60 recipe positions of 30 steps each, weekly brew scheduling, a brewing log and remote maintenance over a network connection, built almost entirely on Siemens components; and BrauKon TControl for brewhouse steps such as mashing, lautering and wort boiling, also available with remote maintenance. BrauControl includes self-optimising fuzzy logic lautering control that adjusts rake height, pump speed and sparging, which is classical control engineering and not machine learning. BrauKon makes no AI claim.

name: Orise
ai_use_case: anomaly detection and asset health monitoring on brewery production lines
short_description: Orise is a German industrial automation, digitalisation and optimisation firm that absorbed the brewery engineering expertise of Rolec Prozess- und Brautechnik as Rolec winds down through liquidation in 2026, and now sells a Brewery Optimization Services line. Its named digital products include Performance Monitor, Lean Shopfloor Manager, Asset Health Monitoring, and a Manufacturing AI line covering Anomaly Detection, Micro-Stop Detection and custom AI solutions. Orise states plainly that this was a transfer of people and know-how, not an acquisition of the Rolec business. The AI claim sits in the Manufacturing AI product line rather than in the brewery process control itself.

name: Parsec
ai_use_case: algorithmic fermentation kinetics control and nutrient dosing
short_description: Parsec builds automation and control systems for wineries, covering micro-oxygenation, fermentation control, selective extraction and real-time monitoring, with patented technology installed in more than 30 countries. Its named products are the SAEn5000 monitoring and vinification automation platform, ADCF (dynamic analysis of fermentation kinetics), which measures CO2 output continuously to track sugar consumption and flag slowdowns or stuck fermentations, EVO2FERM, which adapts yeast nutrient additions in real time, and Aphromate for sparkling wine prise de mousse. Parsec describes these as intelligent algorithms developed experimentally; there is no machine learning claim. Parsec is being acquired by Enartis.

name: Wine Technology Incorporated (VinWizard)
ai_use_case: winery tank and cellar process control
short_description: Wine Technology Incorporated sells VinWizard, a winery automation, monitoring and control system used by over 200 wineries, with a second base in Marlborough, New Zealand. It controls tank temperature, automated pumpovers, air injection, headspace gassing and agitators, reads in-tank sensors for temperature stratification, brix and redox, and extends to chillers, barrel and case goods rooms, CO2, water and power. Its IOWIZ-4 and IOWIZ-16 IO controllers have been built in-house since 2016, and CellarView is a browser-based digital tank board. Alerts go out by email or SMS when tanks drift out of range. No AI or machine learning claim is made.

name: CARL GmbH
ai_use_case: distilling process control and automatic fractionation
short_description: CARL GmbH, the Christian Carl still works founded in 1869, builds pot stills and distillation plants for craft and commercial distilleries worldwide. Its named control products are DPC 510 (Distilling Process Control), a 20 inch touchscreen system regulating heating and cooling, temperature monitoring, safety interlocks and automatic fractionation with recipe management; the compact DPC 200/210 TOUCH with optional remote access for retrofitting older CARL stills; CADi (Computer Aided Distilling) with integrated flow and alcohol measurement for fully automatic runs; and DPC 50, a calculator that works out dilution water and duty. CARL makes no AI or machine learning claim; this is recipe-driven process control and the origin point of distillery process data.

name: ABE Beverage Equipment (American Beer Equipment)
ai_use_case: brewhouse assisted brewing automation
short_description: ABE Beverage Equipment, formerly American Beer Equipment and a division of Norland International, builds brewhouses, fermentation, grain handling and canning lines for craft breweries. Its named control offering is the Brewhouse Automation Plus assisted brewing package, standard on new brewhouses, which automates liquor blending, vorlauf and wort grant, sparge control, lauter to kettle and whirlpool transfers, knockout to fermenter at a regulated pitch temperature, and liquor tank management with volumetric auto-stop and remote viewing and control. BrewPilot is its entry-level system for nano and brewpub scale. ABE deliberately uses off-the-shelf automation components and makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: ZoomAgri
ai_use_case: computer vision barley varietal purity and grain quality grading
total_raised: USD 9.3 million (USD 3.3 million Series A plus a USD 6 million round backed by GrainCorp)
short_description: ZoomAgri sells scanner devices plus software that identify barley varieties and grade physical grain quality from images, described on its own site as computer vision and machine learning delivered as vision as a service. Malting barley is a core commodity: the site cites MEBAK approval for barley varietal purity and Syndicat de Paris and Bipea testing for malting barley. Grain Trade Australia endorsed ZoomAgri One for varietal purity assessment in the Barley Trading Standards from the 2026-27 crop year, and GrainCorp has bought more than 40 devices for its east coast sites and ports. This is the clearest verified machine learning claim on the malt and barley raw material layer.

name: Fermentis
ai_use_case: machine learning prediction of yeast contribution to beer aroma
short_description: Fermentis is the beverage fermentation arm of Lesaffre, selling active dry yeasts, bacteria and fermentation aids to brewers, winemakers, distillers, cider makers and mead makers under the SafBrew, SafOeno and SafSpirit lines. Its own corporate news reports a Sensory Machine Learning project run by Fermentis Academy with Lesaffre Group R&D that trained models on analytical and sensory datasets to explore and predict how yeast strains shape the aromatic profiles of beer, and which won an award at Lesaffre's first Digital, Data and Tech awards. The work is presented as an internal R&D project rather than a product brewers can buy today.

name: Berkeley Yeast
ai_use_case: synthetic biology strain engineering for flavour, no machine learning claim
short_description: Berkeley Yeast is a UC Berkeley spinout that uses synthetic biology to engineer brewing and wine yeast strains, selling FRESH low diacetyl strains, TROPICS and SUPERBLOOM thiol releasing strains for hop-like aroma, SUMMERSTONE, the GALACTIC souring strain and non-alcoholic beer strains in dry and liquid formats. It was co-founded by Charles Denby, Nick Harris and Rachel Li with UC Berkeley professor Jay Keasling as key inventor, and is funded by NSF, NIH and USDA grants plus venture capital. Its own website makes no machine learning claim: the AI angle in press coverage belongs to a separate Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory project using the ART Bayesian recommendation tool to tune hop-flavour metabolite production, which does not name the company. Included as the flagship engineered-strain supplier on the ingredient layer, with the AI claim explicitly not attributed to it.
key_people: Charles Denby (Co-founder), Nick Harris (Co-founder), Rachel Li (Co-founder)

name: Renaissance BioScience
ai_use_case: ai assisted wild yeast strain discovery from genomic and phenotypic data
total_raised: CAD 550,000 GeneSolve grant from Genome BC for this project
short_description: Renaissance BioScience is a Vancouver yeast bioengineering company whose Food and Beverages solutions cover wine, cider, beer and distilled spirits. In February 2026 it announced a 24 month, 550,000 dollar Genome BC GeneSolve project with Dr Vivien Measday at the University of British Columbia to build a proprietary wild yeast discovery platform, characterising more than 700 natural strains and combining metagenomics with AI to identify commercially valuable traits faster than conventional screening. The announced commercial focus of the platform is waste valorisation and industrial compounds, not brewing or wine, so the AI work is adjacent to beverage rather than aimed at it today.
key_people: John Husnik (Co-CEO and Chief Scientific Officer)

name: Hopsteiner
ai_use_case: genomics assisted hop breeding, no machine learning claim
short_description: Hopsteiner, trading as Simon H. Steiner Hopfen GmbH, is a sixth generation global hop supplier of varieties, pellets and extracts, founded in 1845 and headquartered in Mainburg, Germany with US operations. Its research and development function under Dr Martin Biendl runs a breeding program for drought, heat and pest tolerant cultivars and novel flavour profiles, with partners including the Fraunhofer Institute and the Technical University of Munich, and the company has published chromosome-scale haplotype-resolved hop genome assemblies to support genomics-assisted breeding. Its own R and D pages make no machine learning or AI claim: the work described is genomics and conventional breeding science. Included because the hop breeding layer is otherwise absent from the database.
key_people: Martin Biendl (Head of Research and Development and Analytics)
